preconditions.description: The number of vertices n is between 1 and 300,000 inclusive.
The number of edges m is between 0 and 300,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u_i <= n and 1 <= v_i <= n and u_i != v_i and 1 <= w_i <= 10**9 for u_i, v_i, w_i in edges)
preconditions.description: Each edge connects two distinct vertices within the valid range and has a positive integer weight up to 10^9.
The start vertex u is a valid vertex index.
The graph is guaranteed to be connected.

preconditions.expression: len(set((min(u_i, v_i), max(u_i, v_i)) for u_i, v_i, _ in edges)) == m
preconditions.description: There is no more than one edge between any pair of vertices.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly n-1 edges, forming a tree structure.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= idx <= m for idx in selected_edge_indices)
postconditions.description: All selected edge indices are valid and within the input range.
All selected edge indices are distinct.
The selected edges form a shortest-path tree from the start vertex, meaning the distance from start_vertex to any other vertex in the tree equals the shortest distance in the original graph.

postconditions.expression: total_weight == sum(edges[idx-1][2] for idx in selected_edge_indices)
postconditions.description: The printed total weight equals the sum of weights of the selected edges.
The total weight of the selected edges is the minimum possible among all valid shortest-path trees from the start vertex.
